unmutated.K1:hmac-rfc4231: Not targeted by any entry: NoOpKeyedRandom is the only fixture that touches the hash and MAC, and it fails K1:sha256-vectors first (its digest is zeros). A MAC written wrongly (a key longer than the 64-byte block not hashed first, ipad and opad swapped, the wrong block size) is a realistic mistake that RFC 4231 cases 1 to 7 catch, and K2:matches-jdk would catch it too, but no entry breaks hmacSha256 alone; this allowance is a gap in the matrix, not a claim that the law is unreachable.
unmutated.K2:derive-is-sha256: Not targeted: the keyed fixtures override draw and the encoding fixtures re-encode, but none changes how derive reads the digest. A derive that takes the last 8 bytes, or reads the first 8 little-endian, would pass K3 (it still separates domains and fields) and K5, and would silently change every published salt, eclipse and deal seed; only this label's comparison with the JDK's SHA-256 of the encoding catches it. A gap in the matrix, not an unreachable law.
unmutated.K2:draw-is-hmac: Not targeted: UnkeyedDraw, ShortKeyDraw, KeyXorDraw, LenientKeyDraw and StatefulDraw each break draw but are all caught earlier by their own K4 or K7 label, and the encoding fixtures change only the bytes MAC'd. A draw that reads the MAC's first 8 bytes little-endian, or keys the MAC but over a different slice of the encoding, keeps every K4, K5 and K7 label green and is caught only by comparing with the JDK's HMAC here. A gap in the matrix, not an unreachable law.
unmutated.K2:matches-jdk: Not targeted: no entry breaks sha256 or hmacSha256 across lengths. It restates K1 over every input length 0 to 300 and key lengths 1 to 200, which is what catches a padding bug at a block boundary (55, 56, 63 or 64 bytes) or a long-key bug that the fixed K1 vectors may not reach; it is also the second net under K1:hmac-rfc4231. A gap in the matrix, not an unreachable law.
unmutated.K6:uniform: A statistical positive control on the reference, not a check on a separate seam. A draw that is not uniform must differ from HMAC-SHA-256 (caught by K1 and K2) or its unit must not be the high 53 bits (K5:high-bits and K5:range), or its odds must be inexact (K5:edges-exact); whatever else fails K6 already fails one of those, so no distinct realistic mutant exists whose only failure is the chi-squared. The label guards that the sample sizes and tolerances of the harness itself stay sound on the reference.
